title: Relative fibre-associated primes of a projective module meet the closed fibre over a local base
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ (the nonunits of $R$ form this proper ideal), let $R\to C$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, and let $P$ be a $C$-module. Assume $P$ is projective as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], $C/\mathfrak mC$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $P/\mathfrak mP$ is a finite $C/\mathfrak mC$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset C$, let $\mathfrak p$ be its inverse image in $R$ and let $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ be the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. If $\mathfrak q$ is an element-annihilator associated prime of the $C$-module $P\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], then $\mathfrak q+\mathfrak mC\ne C$. Here $\mathfrak mC$ is the ideal generated by the images of elements of $\mathfrak m$, and $\mathfrak mP$ is the submodule generated by their products with elements of $P$. No finite generation over $R$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $\overline P=P/\mathfrak mP$ and $\Sigma=\{s\in C:s:\overline P\to\overline P\text{ is injective}\}$. The identity is injective and composites of injective maps are injective, so $\Sigma$ is multiplicative. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], $P$ is flat over $R$, with no finite-generation assumption on $P$ over $R$.

source.place: Tag 05FV (lemma-explain-why-pure), first sentence; hypotheses for Tag 05FQ (lemma-universally-injective-local).

proof.text: For each $s\in\Sigma$, multiplication $u_s:P\to P$ is $R$-linear because the $C$-action commutes with the $R$-action. Its reduction modulo $\mathfrak m$ is injective by the definition of $\Sigma$. Apply [lem-trf-local-universal-injective-residue] with source and target both $P$: the source is projective by hypothesis, the target is flat by step 1, and $R$ is local. Thus $\mathrm{id}_L\otimes u_s$ is injective for every $R$-module $L$. In particular, multiplication by $s$ on $F=P\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is injective. To check the order of factors explicitly, the tensor universal property gives inverse flip maps $x\otimes y\mapsto y\otimes x$; they conjugate $\mathrm{id}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\otimes u_s$ to $u_s\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}$. On a pure tensor the latter is $x\otimes a\mapsto sx\otimes a$, precisely the induced $C$-action; equality holds everywhere since pure tensors generate.

source.place: Tag 05FV (lemma-explain-why-pure), universal-injectivity argument, using Tag 05FR (lemma-invert-universally-injective), whose scalar-map assertion follows from Tag 05FQ (lemma-universally-injective-local).

proof.text: By the exact-annihilator definition, choose $z\in F$ with $\mathfrak q=\operatorname{Ann}_C(z)$. Since $\mathfrak q$ is proper, $z\ne0$: the annihilator of zero contains $1$. If $s\in\mathfrak q\cap\Sigma$, then $sz=0$, contradicting the injectivity of multiplication by $s$ from step 2. Consequently $\mathfrak q\cap\Sigma=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 05FV (lemma-explain-why-pure), the sentence that the fibre-associated prime corresponds to a prime of the localization, expanded via its annihilator witness.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding], disjointness from $\Sigma$ puts $\mathfrak q$ in the contraction image of $\operatorname{Spec}(\Sigma^{-1}C)$. Apply [lem-sfb-fibre-regular-localization-spectrum] with $A=R$, $B=C$, $N=P$: its closed-fibre ring is $C/\mathfrak mC$, Noetherian by hypothesis, its closed-fibre module is $\overline P$, finite by hypothesis, and its multiplicative subset is exactly $\Sigma$. Its spectrum description gives $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak q^{\prime}$ for some $\mathfrak q^{\prime}\in\operatorname{Ass}_C(\overline P)$.

source.place: Tag 05FV (lemma-explain-why-pure), last two sentences, using Tag 05DE (lemma-homothety-spectrum).

proof.text: Choose $w\in\overline P$ with $\mathfrak q^{\prime}=\operatorname{Ann}_C(w)$. Every image of $r\in\mathfrak m$ acts as zero on $\overline P=P/\mathfrak mP$; hence the ideal $\mathfrak mC$ generated by these images is contained in $\mathfrak q^{\prime}$. Therefore $\mathfrak q+\mathfrak mC\subseteq\mathfrak q^{\prime}\ne C$, as required.
